sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- write: Create or overwrite files
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text: Generate an animated SVG of an anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles.

content.thinking:
Let's create an SVG with SMIL animations.

Write a file.

Design: anteater body, snout, unicycle wheel rotating, juggled bottles (3) arcing up and down.

Let me write reasonably careful SVG.

Animation approach: use SMIL <animateTransform> and <animate>.

Let me build a scene 800x600, ground line.

Unicycle: wheel centered (400, 470) radius 90, with spokes rotating. Seat post, saddle. Anteater sits on saddle at ~(400, 300) facing right.

Anteater: body ellipse, long snout, small ears, legs on pedals.

Juggling bottles: three bottles on arcs above anteater's hands, ~ (400,120) area. Use animateMotion along arc paths with staggered begin times.

Let's write.

Bottle symbol: define <g id="bottle"> with body and neck and cap, drawn at origin centered.

Arc paths for juggling: use paths like M 300,180 Q 400,60 500,180 (ballistic-ish). Three bottles with different offsets: one on left arc, one center, one right, staggered timing.

Simpler: each bottle follows a loop path (ellipse-ish) around juggling area, with different begin offsets, making it look like juggling. Path for bottle 1: M330,200 Q400,70 470,200 Q400,330 330,200 Z — closed loop. Actually juggling is more like toss arcs. But a loop reads as juggling acceptable.

Better: toss arcs: bottle goes up and comes down in different hand positions. Let's do 3 paths:
- A: M 280,230 Q 340,40 400,230 (up-down) — but need return. Use path with two quadratics forming a closed loop of the toss from left hand to right hand: M280,230 Q330,60 400,200 Q470,60 520,230 Q460,150 400,180 Q340,150 280,230? Hmm.

Simplest visually pleasing: three bottles each on a closed loop path of a tilted ellipse, offset in phase, so they circle around. Plus rotate slightly. That's classic "juggling" abstraction. But real juggling = toss and catch.

I'll do: bottle A follows path P1 = "M300,220 Q340,60 460,120 Q520,160 460,220 Q380,270 300,220 Z" eh messy.

Let me do proper toss arcs with three separate tosses at different phases, each arc being: rise from hand height, apex, descend to other hand height. Path for one toss: M 320,210 Q 360,70 400,210? That's up and back to same x. Use: M320,210 Q340,70 400,190 then continues down to... To make a continuous loop, path: M320,210 Q350,60 400,190 Q450,320 470,210 Q440,80 320,210? Getting complicated but the trick: a closed path made of two parabolas gives a perpetual toss-and-catch motion.

Closed loop path for toss:
M 320,215 Q 355,60 400,215 Q 445,60 480,215 Q 440,240 400,215? no.

Do: Path = M320,215 Q350,55 400,215 Q450,55 480,215 L480,215 ... not closed.

Alternative approach: each bottle animates y position with values list and x with values list, plus rotation. That's easiest to control.

Bottle A (toss 1): x: 320;400;480 ;320 (goes left->right while up then down?) Let's use keyTimes to make arc: x values "320;400;480;320" with y "215;70;215;215"? Hmm.

Honestly, a nice approach: each bottle moves along a parabola arc alternating between two catch points, using animateTransform translate with values:
Bottle1: (320,215) -> (480,215) via apex (400,60): use values "320,215;400,60;480,215;400,60;320,215" with keyTimes 0;0.25;0.5;0.75;1 and calcMode spline — that makes it bounce back and forth. Nice and simple. Three bottles with different begin offsets and slightly different x ranges so they don't overlap perfectly.

Bottle1: x 280..470, apex y 70
Bottle2: x 330..520, apex y 60
Bottle3: x 300..490, apex y 85

But all three would appear simultaneously overlapping the region — with staggered phases it looks like juggling. Also hands: anteater's two hands at (300,230) and (490,230) doing a circular motion (arms rotate) — animate arms rotation.

Actually let's make it 3 bottles with durations 1.4s, 1.6s, 1.8s, phase offsets 0, -0.5, -0.25. Good enough visually.

Let's construct SVG.

Colors: tan/brown anteater, black diagonal stripe, cream snout. Wheel black with white spokes.

Coordinates:
- Ground y=560.
- Wheel center (400,470), r=95. Tire outer r=95, rim r=80, hub r=10.
- Fork from hub up to seatpost: line (400,470) to (400,300)? Seat post: from (400,470) angled back: seat at (380,250). Let's put saddle at (385,255).
- Anteater sits on saddle: body centered (395,215)? But juggling area above at y 60-230 would overlap. Put anteater lower: saddle at (385,320). Then body above: body ellipse at (395,270) size 120x70. Legs from body down to pedals at (400,470)±.

But juggling needs space above anteater's head. Anteater head at (480,235) facing right with snout extending to (570,255). Juggling space: above head, y 40..200, x 250..520. Head at 235 so ok, juggling region above.

Hmm body at (395,270) and juggle region bottom at 215 overlapping body top (270-35=235). Slight overlap fine—hands up.

Let's set:
- Wheel center (400,500) r=95 (ground at 595, canvas 640?). Let's make viewBox 0 0 800 640, ground y=595.
- Fork: from hub (400,500) to (400,340); seat post (400,340) to saddle (390,320).
- Saddle: rounded rect at (365,310) w=55 h=14.
- Anteater body: ellipse cx=380 cy=285 rx=85 ry=45, slight tilt.
- Head: at (480,250) circle r=28, snout: long cone from (495,245) to (585,270) tapering.
- Ears: small circles at (465,225) and (495,222).
- Eye at (500,243).
- Legs: from body bottom (370,320) to knee (350,400) to pedal (370,470) front; other leg opposite. Feet on pedals which rotate with wheel: pedal at angle. Put crank at wheel center (400,500) r=30, pedals at (400,470) and (400,530). Feet attach there. Simplify: legs drawn as paths ending at pedal positions that move with crank — animate legs? Use a group rotated about (400,500) for the crank+pedals, and legs drawn as static-ish tapered paths to two pedal spots (the crank rotation makes pedals move; legs static looks off). Compromise: keep legs static drawn to pedal at (400,470) and (400,530) and rotate the crank group so pedals rotate—legs won't follow. Alternatively animate leg paths with SMIL 'd' animation? d animation is supported in SVG 1.1 SMIL? 'd' is animatable in SVG2/Chrome yes (Chrome supports animating 'd' for path with same structure). Risky.

Easier: Make feet on pedals static: crank rotates with pedals but we draw feet as children of the rotating crank group (feet rotate too - looks odd but stylized ok). Actually feet fixed to pedal is correct physically; if foot is child of crank group it rotates with pedal—that's right! Pedal stays horizontal though. Draw pedal as rect rotating? Fine: pedal group rotates, we counter-rotate the foot shape? Keep simple: crank group rotates with two pedals (small circles) and the feet drawn as part of it, counter-rotating shoe shapes via their own animateTransform rotate about the pedal center with reverse timing. Doable: shoe at pedal with animateTransform type rotate values "0;360" ... reverse: rotate about pedal center by -angle. Since the shoe's local coords centered on pedal, apply rotate -angle about pedal point. Use nested g translate to pedal then inner g animateTransform rotate 0->-360.

Simpler: skip shoes, just legs drawn to two fixed pedal points and crank rotates—pedal circles orbit and feet stay. Slight cheat, acceptable? I'd rather animate legs. Let's animate legs with animate on 'd'? Chrome supports d animation. I'll use static legs to positions that are the average of pedal cycle: pedal positions at (400,500±30). Foot at (400,470) and (400,530) at that instant; legs look like they reach down to wheel—visually fine since the crank ring rotates visibly. Many cartoons do this.

Actually cutest: the anteater's legs go straight down to pedals drawn as small ellipses that orbit; legs drawn to (400,470)/(400,530) but the crank group rotation moves pedals... mismatch visible.

Alternative: legs both on same pedal point at front (400,468), pedal group rotating. Draw the crank group containing pedals; also draw legs whose 'd' animates between two shapes (one for each pedal) using animate d — I'll do that, Chrome supports it. Let me define two leg paths with same command structure:

Leg A (to front pedal at angle -90°, i.e., (400,470)): M 355,315 Q 330,395 385,462
Leg B (to back pedal at (400,530)): M 375,320 Q 395,420 405,522
These have same structure (M Q). Animate d between them with values A;B;A... and keyTimes matching crank rotation. Crank rotates 360 over 2s, pedals swap every 1s. So animate leg d values "A;B;A" dur="2s" and the other leg "B;A;B".

Also feet at end. Good.

Arms: two arms from body up doing juggling; animate rotation about shoulder. Shoulder front (455,265), back (330,270). Rotate arm groups ±25° sinusoidally. Hands at end of arms ~ (490,190) and (300,200). Juggling bottles caught around those heights: use hand points for the arc endpoints.

Juggling: hand A at (500,195), hand B at (310,200). Bottle toss arcs: from A up to apex and back to A? Real juggling: throw from right hand, catch in left, etc. Simplify: bottles oscillate along an arc between hand positions.

Let's define three bottles each with translate animation values along parabola between left and right points:
B1: (310,200) -> (500,200) apex (405,70): values "310,200;405,70;500,200;405,70;310,200" dur 1.6s.
B2: (340,190) -> (520,190) apex (430,50): dur 1.9s begin "-0.63s".
B3: (290,205) -> (470,205) apex (380,85): dur 1.5s begin "-0.3s".

Each bottle also rotates (animateTransform rotate) with values "0;180;360" for tumble.

But multiple animateTransform on same element need additive="sum". Bottle group: outer g with translate animation (type translate), inner g with rotate animation.

Bottle design: at origin, body rect x=-10 y=-26 w=20 h=34 rx=5, neck rect x=-6 y=-38 w=12 h=14, cap rect x=-7 y=-42 w=14 h=6. Colors: green glass.

Also a juggly highlight/ground shadow.

Background: sky gradient, ground, some clouds, maybe audience.

Also add title? Not needed.

Let's write the SVG.

Spokes: 8 lines through center, animated rotating with the wheel group.

Also add subtle bobbing to whole anteater? Could add slight rotate of body group. Keep.

Let's also add motion: unicycle rolling? Keep stationary, maybe slight wheel rotation only.

Write file animate.svg.

Also add CSS fallback? SMIL fine.

Let me write code carefully.

Sun/clouds optional, add simple.

Coordinate check for arms: shoulder front (450,270) arm length to hand (500,195): path M450,270 Q 480,225 500,195 with hand circle r=10 at end. Rotate group about (450,270) by -20..20.

Back arm: shoulder (320,275), hand (300,200)? path M320,275 Q295,235 305,200, hand at (305,200). Hmm hand positions: left hand around x=310 y=200 matches B arcs left ends ~290-340. Right hand at (500,195) matches right ends 470-520. Good.

But bottles at left end (310,200) should be at the hand (305,200). ok.

Now unicycle wheel must be below; juggling bottles around y 50-200, above head (head at 250 with snout to 285 x). Bottle right end x=520,y=190 near head top (head top ~222). ok.

Juggle region x 290-520 y 50-205. Anteater body center x 380, top of body 285-45=240. Good clearance.

Write it.

Let's produce final SVG file path: /Users/andie/Downloads/.../work/anteater-juggling-unicycle.svg

I'll write with nice formatting.

Crank: g transform rotate about (400,500): contains crank arms and pedals. Pedal at (400,472) and (400,528) i.e. ±28 from center. Crank arm lines from center to those points.

Pedals drawn as small rounded rects that stay horizontal: put each pedal in its own group with counter-rotation: outer g rotate(θ) about center, inner g at translate(0,-28) with rotate(-θ). Implement with nested animateTransform: pedal group A: <g transform="translate(400,500)"><g><animateTransform type rotate 0->360 dur 2s repeatCount indefinite/> ... hmm nested rotate about (0,0) of translated frame.

Structure:
<g transform="translate(400,500)">
  <g id="crank">
    <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate" from="0" to="360" dur="2s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="-28" .../>

</g>
Wait counter-rotation must be opposite sign of crank rotation; crank rotates 0->360, counter should be 0->-360. But these pedals are children of crank group which already rotates them; the inner counter cancels. LegA: "M 360,318 Q 335,400 390,462" (to front pedal top)

arguments.content:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"
     viewBox="0 0 800 640" width="800" height="640" role="img"
     aria-label="Animated anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles">

  <title>Anteater on a Unicycle, Juggling Bottles</title>

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="sky" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#bfe9ff"/>
      <stop offset="60%" stop-color="#e8f7ff"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#fff6e0"/>
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="fur" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#c98f57"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#a9703f"/>
    </linearGradient>

    <linearGradient id="snout" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#f3e3c9"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#d9c39f"/>
    </linearGradient>

    <radialGradient id="groundShade" cx="0.5" cy="0.5" r="0.5">
      <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.35"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </radialGradient>

    <!-- a bottle drawn around the origin -->
    <g id="bottle">
      <rect x="-11" y="-22" width="22" height="38" rx="6" fill="currentColor"/>
      <rect x="-11" y="-22" width="22" height="38" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" opacity="0.18"/>
      <rect x="-6" y="-36" width="12" height="16" fill="currentColor"/>
      <rect x="-8" y="-42" width="16" height="8" rx="2" fill="#3b3b3b"/>
      <rect x="-7" y="-12" width="14" height="14" rx="2" fill="#fdfdfd" opacity="0.85"/>
      <rect x="-9" y="-16" width="4" height="18" rx="2" fill="#ffffff" opacity="0.45"/>
    </g>

    <g id="cloud">
      <ellipse cx="0"   cy="0"   rx="42" ry="22" fill="#ffffff"/>
      <ellipse cx="38"  cy="6"   rx="32" ry="18" fill="#ffffff"/>
      <ellipse cx="-36" cy="8"   rx="28" ry="16" fill="#ffffff"/>
    </g>
  </defs>

  <!-- ================= BACKGROUND ================= -->
  <rect width="800" height="640" fill="url(#sky)"/>

  <g opacity="0.9">
    <use xlink:href="#cloud" transform="translate(140,90) scale(1.1)">
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate"
        values="140,90; 900,90" dur="70s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    </use>
    <use xlink:href="#cloud" transform="translate(600,150) scale(0.8)" opacity="0.75">
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate"
        values="600,150; 1360,150" dur="95s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
    </use>
  </g>

  <circle cx="690" cy="90" r="42" fill="#ffe08a" opacity="0.85">
    <animate attributeName="opacity" values="0.85;0.6;0.85" dur="6s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
  </circle>

  <rect x="0" y="595" width="800" height="45" fill="#8fc98a"/>
  <rect x="0" y="595" width="800" height="8" fill="#79b574"/>
  <ellipse cx="400" cy="600" rx="190" ry="26" fill="url(#groundShade)"/>

  <!-- ================= JUGGLING BOTTLES ================= -->
  <g id="juggling">
    <!-- bottle 1 -->
    <g>
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate"
        values="310,200; 405,70; 500,200; 405,70; 310,200"
        keyTimes="0;0.25;0.5;0.75;1" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite"
        calcMode="spline" keySplines="0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1"/>
      <g>
        <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate"
          values="0;180;360" dur="1.6s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
        <use xlink:href="#bottle" color="#4caf50"/>
      </g>
    </g>

    <!-- bottle 2 -->
    <g>
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate"
        values="340,190; 430,48; 520,190; 430,48; 340,190"
        keyTimes="0;0.25;0.5;0.75;1" dur="1.9s" begin="-0.63s" repeatCount="indefinite"
        calcMode="spline" keySplines="0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1"/>
      <g>
        <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate"
          values="30;210;390" dur="1.9s" begin="-0.63s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
        <use xlink:href="#bottle" color="#3f8fd6"/>
      </g>
    </g>

    <!-- bottle 3 -->
    <g>
      <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate"
        values="295,205; 380,88; 468,205; 380,88; 295,205"
        keyTimes="0;0.25;0.5;0.75;1" dur="1.5s" begin="-0.28s" repeatCount="indefinite"
        calcMode="spline" keySplines="0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1;0.4 0 0.6 1"/>
      <g>
        <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="rotate"
          values="0;180;360" dur="1.5s" begin="-0.28s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
        <use xlink:href="#bottle" color="#e0a233"/>
      </g>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- ================= UNICYCLE ================= -->
  <g id="unicycle">
    <!-- fork / seat post -->
    <path d="M400,500 L400,352" stroke="#9aa4ad" stroke-width="12" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/>
    <path d="M400,500 L400,352" stroke="#c3ccd3" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"/>
    <path d="M392,352 L392,330" stroke="#7d8791" stroke-width="10" stroke-linecap="round"/>
